Jordan (customer): Hey team — hitting a 413 from the rerank endpoint when we send ~600 docs. Response: `413 Payload Too Large` with body 'input too large'. No further detail. Can you advise?
Amy: @Jordan thanks — can you paste the exact curl + body (sanitized) so we can repro? Is this for /v1/rerank or a custom route?
Jordan (customer): /v1/rerank. Here's a sanitized snippet: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"long user query...", "docs":[{"id":"1","text":"..."}, ..., {"id":"600","text":"..."}]}'```
Amy: Got it. Do you know approx tokens per doc? Also did you try reducing docs to ~100 to see if it succeeds?
Jordan (customer): Average doc ~1200 chars, query ~300 chars. Reducing to 100 docs returns 200 OK and scores back. So seems like a docs-count/size limit.
Marco: looping in eng — @Marco here. We see 413s for two distinct reasons: request body bytes > N and an internal token-sum check that rejects if total_tokens > MAX_TOKENS_PER_RERANK. The error message currently lumps both into 'input too large' which is ambiguous.
Marco: Can you attach the raw response body and the request-id header if present? That helps us map to logs.
Jordan (customer): response body was just `{ "error": "input too large" }`, no request-id in headers on their end (they're using an API gateway).
Amy: Thanks. We should escalate — this is a UX/breaking issue. @Maya can we update error wording to include which limit hit (body-bytes vs token-sum vs docs-count) and include limit values and a short mitigation hint? e.g., `input too large: total_docs=600 > max_docs=200` or `input too large: total_tokens=245000 > max_tokens=200000`
Maya: +1. From product: error should be actionable. We should include numeric limits and a link to docs. I can spec the message: `error: input too large; reason=docs_count; max_docs=200; see https://docs.redwood.ai/rerank-limits`
Marco: For immediate triage, eng can add a short-term improvement in the response body with reason code. Long-term we'd prefer the client SDK to pre-check and provide tooling to chunk.
Priya: noted for infra — I'll search logs for request time range around `1749998000` and any gateway stripping of request-id. If we can find the internal request-id we can return it back.
Amy: Jordan, short-term workaround: chunk docs into batches of 150-200, call rerank per batch, then merge scores. We can share a helper snippet. Example: ```python
# naive chunk
for i in range(0, len(docs), 150):
  batch = docs[i:i+150]
  resp = client.rerank(query, batch)
  collect(resp.scores)
```
Jordan (customer): Can you also confirm whether characters or tokens are counted? Their app does pre-tokenization on server side so they'd like to know which metric to use when chunking.
Marco: It's token-based for the internal ranking model. Character counts are approximate. We'll add a short note to the API: `limits measured in tokens (approx via byte-level BPE) and docs count`.
Maya: I'll create a short doc update and a concise FAQ blurb about chunking patterns + sample code.
Marco: Action items: 1) eng add reason code to 413 responses (docs_count|body_bytes|token_sum) and include offending values. 2) product update docs and add chunking snippet. 3) support send workaround + timeline to customer.
Amy: I'll follow up with Jordan in-thread once we have an ETA (aiming same-day for the response wording tweak; docs update tomorrow).
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: canary v1.2.3 -> 3 hosts (note: this is unrelated to rerank fix) :rocket:
Amy: Thanks all — Jordan, we appreciate the report. We'll circle back with the ETA and a helper script. :thumbsup:
